questions.q: Why can't MERGE be called directly as a writeStream sink?
options: MERGE is a table-level SQL/DeltaTable operation, not a built-in streaming sink — there's no .mergeStream() method
MERGE only works on batch DataFrames that have never been read with readStream
MERGE is deprecated and no longer usable at all
writeStream doesn't support any transformation logic whatsoever
questions.explain: foreachBatch is the bridge that makes MERGE usable within a streaming pipeline.

options: Hands each arriving micro-batch to an ordinary Python function as a regular, static DataFrame, where any normal batch operation works
Automatically merges every micro-batch without any custom logic
Deletes each micro-batch after processing it
Only works with SQL, never PySpark functions
questions.explain: Inside that function, MERGE works exactly as it always has on a static DataFrame.

questions.q: How does the cleaning logic inside foreachBatch relate to earlier lessons?
options: It's exactly Lesson 27's cleaning logic combined with Lesson 22's MERGE call — nothing new in the logic itself
It requires an entirely new set of transformation functions unique to streaming
It can only use SQL, never withColumn or dropDuplicates
It bypasses casting and deduplication entirely
questions.explain: The genuinely new piece is only the streaming wrapper (foreachBatch) around already-known logic.

questions.q: How does this lesson's streaming pipeline differ from Lesson 29's scheduled batch pipeline?
options: It can process new bronze rows within minutes, continuously or on-demand, rather than waiting for the next scheduled run
It processes data less frequently than the scheduled version
It cannot use MERGE at all, only append
There's no real functional difference between the two
questions.explain: This is genuinely real-time, not just "runs more often" than a daily schedule.

questions.q: What feeds bronze.trips as the streaming source in this pipeline?
options: Autoloader, from Lesson 32, continuously picking up new files
A manual spark.read.csv() call run once
Unity Catalog's access control system
A separate relational database unrelated to Delta
questions.explain: readStream then treats that continuously-fed bronze table as a growing, unbounded table.
